method: HubSpot MCP query_crm_data (read-only). Followed tool_guidance: property names confirmed with search_properties/get_properties. COUNT(hs_object_id) is executed by the engine as SUM of record IDs (wrong); every count was re-run with COUNT(*) and only COUNT(*) results are used as facts. Association existence filters (associations.X IS NULL) are honoured in plain COUNT(*) queries (cross-checked: NULL + NOT NULL complements add up to the object totals) but are silently dropped in GROUP BY aggregate queries and in the first single-filter COUNT(hs_object_id) attempts. No write tool was called.

pipeline_labels.note: Labels come verbatim from query_crm_data GROUP BY pipeline output. Only 5 pipelines hold deals; the SEALSQ property resource (2026-09-14) says the portal has 7 deal pipelines, so 2 pipelines are empty or not surfaced by the query engine.

gaps: Pipeline labels: the SQL engine surfaced only 5 pipelines with deals (IDs 12096408, 13772279, 40296576, 705868909, 766126206); the SEALSQ property resource says 7 deal pipelines exist. No read-only pipelines endpoint was available among the loaded tools, so the 2 remaining pipeline names/IDs are not measured here (map from SEALSQ_Property_Resource.md stage-ID section if needed).

Per-pipeline split of the 116 'final_customer but no company' deals could not be measured: GROUP BY pipeline silently drops the associations.COMPANY IS NULL filter (returned 1043 = all deals with final_customer). The 10-record sample is 100% SealSQ Hardware, but that is a sample, not a measure.

'IS NOT NULL' on the year fields is not a fill measure (calculated fields evaluate to 0 on every deal: 1972/1972/1964/1972). The '> 0' counts (354 / 403 / 897 / 581) are the usable fill proxy; negative or zero-but-meaningful values would be excluded.

pipeline_2029__k__ is a plain number property while the 2025/2026 fields are calculation-named; whether 2029 is user-entered or calculated was not determinable from get_properties (no calculated flag in the tool output).
First-attempt queries using COUNT(hs_object_id) returned ID sums (engine quirk); all such results were discarded and re-run with COUNT(*). Only COUNT(*) results are reported as facts.
Duplicate clusters and NQL/MQL figures were not re-measured live (no string functions / DISTINCT in the SQL dialect); they remain sourced from the Hs-Logic screenshots (10,000-record cap).
Deals-per-pipeline conversion uses hs_is_closed_won only; hs_is_closed_lost per pipeline was not queried.
Seat usage counts per seat type were not queried (SEATS returns names only; counting would require USER object searches which were out of the read-only scope requested).
